rmt-2006-gen-01.title: Distance and time
rmt-2006-gen-01.body:
Let the route be 3 units. He rides 2 units in time $t$ and walks 1 unit in time $2t$. Riding speed $\frac2t$, walking speed $\frac1{2t}$; the ratio is $\frac{2/t}{1/(2t)}=4$.

**Answer: 4**

rmt-2006-gen-03.title: Impossible
rmt-2006-gen-03.body:
If nine letters are in their own envelopes, the tenth letter must go into the one remaining envelope, which is its own. So exactly nine correct is impossible, and the probability is 0.

**Answer: 0**

rmt-2006-gen-04.title: Count losses
rmt-2006-gen-04.body:
Every game produces exactly one loss. All players except the champion are eliminated, each after 3 losses: $511\cdot3=1533$ losses. The champion can have at most 2 losses without being eliminated. Total games $\le1533+2=1535$, and this is achievable.

**Answer: 1535**

rmt-2006-gen-05.title: Common ratio
rmt-2006-gen-05.body:
The common ratio is $\frac{6!}{5!}=6$. The fourth term is the fifth divided by 6: $\frac{5!}6=\frac{120}6=20$.

**Answer: 20**

rmt-2006-gen-06.title: Rate of the slow clock
rmt-2006-gen-06.body:
In $3\frac12$ hours the alarm clock has lost $14$ minutes, so it now shows 11:46. It runs at $\frac{56}{60}$ of the true rate, so it needs $14\cdot\frac{60}{56}=15$ real minutes to gain its 14 minutes.

**Answer: 15 minutes**

rmt-2006-gen-07.title: Complement
rmt-2006-gen-07.body:
The flight fails only if all three engines fail: $(0.01)^3=10^{-6}$. So $P(\text{success})=1-10^{-6}=0.999999$.

**Answer: 0.999999**

rmt-2006-gen-08.title: List the solutions
rmt-2006-gen-08.body:
We need five positive integers with equal sum and product. With four 1s the sum is $4+x$ and product $x$, impossible; so at most three 1s. Three 1s and $a\le b$: $3+a+b=ab$, i.e. $(a-1)(b-1)=4$, giving $(a,b)=(2,5)$ or $(3,3)$. Two 1s and $a\le b\le c$ all $\ge2$: $2+a+b+c=abc$ gives only $(2,2,2)$ (since $abc\ge4c$ grows too fast). So the three solutions are $\{1,1,1,2,5\}$ (sum 10), $\{1,1,1,3,3\}$ (sum 9) and $\{1,1,2,2,2\}$ (sum 8). The largest sum is 10.

**Answer: $1,1,1,2,5$**

rmt-2006-gen-09.title: Set up an equation
rmt-2006-gen-09.body:
For $\frac ab$, adding $b$ to numerator and denominator gives $\frac{a+b}{2b}$. This equals $k\cdot\frac ab$ when $a+b=2ka$, i.e. $b=(2k-1)a$, so the fraction is $\frac1{2k-1}$: for $k=2$ it is $\frac13$ (the example), for $k=3$ it is $\frac15$, and for $k=4$ it is $\frac17$. Check: $\frac{1+5}{5+5}=\frac35=3\cdot\frac15$ and $\frac{1+7}{7+7}=\frac47=4\cdot\frac17$.

**Answer: $\frac15$ and $\frac17$**

rmt-2006-gen-10.title: Sum of odd numbers
rmt-2006-gen-10.body:
The sum of the first $n$ odd integers is $n^2$ ($1+3+\dots+(2n-1)=n^2$). So the sum is $2006^2$ and its square root is $2006$.

**Answer: 2006**

rmt-2006-gen-13.title: Search
rmt-2006-gen-13.body:
With three signs the digits split into four numbers. Try $123-45-67+89$: $123-45=78$, $78-67=11$, $11+89=100$ ✓.

**Answer: $123-45-67+89=100$**

rmt-2006-gen-14.title: Symmetry
rmt-2006-gen-14.body:
The disk has area $\pi\cdot\pi^2=\pi^3$. The map $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,-y)$ preserves the disk and swaps the regions $y\ge\sin x$ and $y\le\sin x$ (because $\sin$ is odd), so each has half the area: $\frac{\pi^3}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{\pi^3}2$**

rmt-2006-gen-15.title: List the palindromes
rmt-2006-gen-15.body:
The next palindromes after 15951 are $16061,16161,16261$. The third is 16261, which is $16261-15951=310$ miles further. In 5 hours that is $\frac{310}5=62$ mph.

**Answer: 62 mph**

rmt-2006-gen-16.title: Central angles
rmt-2006-gen-16.body:
Triangle $OA_nA_{n+1}$ is isosceles with base angles $35^\circ$, so the central angle $\angle A_nOA_{n+1}=110^\circ$. The condition $A_n\ne A_{n+2}$ means the points keep moving in the same direction around the circle. So $A_n=A_1$ iff $110(n-1)$ is a multiple of 360, i.e. $11(n-1)\equiv0\pmod{36}$. Since $\gcd(11,36)=1$, $36\mid n-1$ and the smallest $n>1$ is $37$.

**Answer: 37**

rmt-2006-gen-17.title: Total time
rmt-2006-gen-17.body:
The cars close the 1-mile gap at $30-20=10$ mph, so they collide after $\frac1{10}$ hour. The fly flies at 40 mph during that time: $40\cdot\frac1{10}=4$ miles.

**Answer: 4 miles**

rmt-2006-gen-18.title: Check after every throw
rmt-2006-gen-18.body:
The order of throws is Brian, Alex, Brian, Alex.

After Brian's first throw Alex has 0 makes, so Brian must have missed: probability $0.4$.

After Alex's first throw, anything is fine. Then Brian's second throw: if Alex made his first (probability 0.8), Brian may do anything (Brian has at most 1). If Alex missed (probability 0.2), Brian must also miss (probability 0.4), and then after Alex's second throw nothing can go wrong. After Alex's second throw in the first case Alex has at least 1 and Brian at most 1, fine.

Probability $=0.4\left(0.8+0.2\cdot0.4\right)=0.4\cdot0.88=0.352=\frac{44}{125}$.

**Answer: $\frac{44}{125}$**

rmt-2006-gen-19.title: Pair $n$ with $999999-n$
rmt-2006-gen-19.body:
Consider $0,1,\dots,999999$ written with six digits (leading zeros do not change the digit sum). The numbers $n$ and $999999-n$ have digits that add to $9$ in each place, so each pair has total digit sum $54$. There are $500000$ pairs: $500000\cdot54=27{,}000{,}000$. The number $0$ adds nothing, and $1{,}000{,}000$ adds $1$. Total $27{,}000{,}001$.

**Answer: 27,000,001**

rmt-2006-gen-22.title: Bayes' theorem
rmt-2006-gen-22.body:
Assuming the two problem sets are finished independently in a given library: $P(\text{both}\mid\text{math lib})=0.95\cdot0.75=0.7125$ and $P(\text{both}\mid\text{chem lib})=0.9\cdot0.8=0.72$. Then $P(\text{math}\mid\text{both})=\frac{0.7125\cdot0.6}{0.7125\cdot0.6+0.72\cdot0.4}=\frac{0.4275}{0.7155}=\frac{95}{159}$.

**Answer: $\frac{95}{159}$**

rmt-2006-gen-23.title: Unfold the reflections
rmt-2006-gen-23.body:
Put the mirrors on the axes. Reflecting the path across the mirrors in turn replaces the bent path by a straight one: reflect $B=(a,b)$ across the $x$-axis to $(a,-b)$ and then across the $y$-axis to $(-a,-b)$. The path $A\to$ mirror $\to$ mirror $\to B$ has the same length as the straight segment from $A=(x,y)$ to $(-a,-b)$, namely $\sqrt{(x+a)^2+(y+b)^2}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{(x+a)^2+(y+b)^2}$**

rmt-2006-gen-25.title: Divisor sum
rmt-2006-gen-25.body:
$S(n)=\frac{\sigma(n)}n$ where $\sigma$ is the sum of divisors (since $\sum\frac1k=\sum\frac{n/k}{n}$). With $2006=2\cdot17\cdot59$: $\sigma=(1+2)(1+17)(1+59)=3\cdot18\cdot60=3240$. So $S(2006)=\frac{3240}{2006}=\frac{1620}{1003}$ (in lowest terms since $1003=17\cdot59$ shares no factor with $1620=2^2\cdot3^4\cdot5$).

**Answer: $\frac{1620}{1003}$**
